target_schema.name: global_healthcare
target_schema.title: Unified Synthea + OMOP CDM target schema

fields.name: care_site_id
fields.description: Organization/care site the provider practices at.

fields.name: organization_id
fields.description: Unique identifier of the organization/care site.

fields.name: location_id
fields.description: Unique identifier of the geographic location.

fields.name: observation_id
fields.description: Unified identifier spanning OMOP observation and measurement facts.

fields.name: immunization_id
fields.description: Synthetic surrogate key; no source counterpart.

fields.name: allergy_id
fields.description: Synthetic surrogate key; no source counterpart.

conflicts.description: The core person entity is named 'patients' in Synthea and 'person' in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target resource 'patient' (snake_case, singular).

conflicts.description: The clinical interaction entity is 'encounters' in Synthea and 'visit_occurrence' in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target resource 'encounter'; related sub-entity visit_detail mapped to 'encounter_detail'.

conflicts.description: Facility/location-of-care entity named 'organizations' vs 'care_site'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target resource 'organization'; OMOP care_site identifiers retained as care_site_* columns/FKs.

conflicts.description: Medication fact named 'medications' vs 'drug_exposure'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target resource 'medication'.

conflicts.description: Procedure fact named 'procedures' vs 'procedure_occurrence'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target resource 'procedure'.

conflicts.description: Condition fact named 'conditions' vs 'condition_occurrence'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target resource 'condition'.

conflicts.description: Synthea 'observations' overlaps both OMOP 'observation' and 'measurement'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into a single target resource 'observation' capturing textual and numeric results.

conflicts.description: Clinician entity uses plural 'providers' vs singular 'provider'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into target resource 'provider'.

conflicts.description: Identifier naming differs: Synthea uses bare 'id', OMOP uses '<entity>_id'.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to snake_case '<entity>_id' surrogate naming across all target tables.

conflicts.description: Synthea imaging_studies columns contain spaces and are not snake_case.
conflicts.resolution: Renamed to snake_case (body_site_code, modality_code, sop_code, etc.).

conflicts.description: Spelling inconsistency: 'speciality' (Synthea) vs 'specialty' (OMOP).
conflicts.resolution: Standardized on 'specialty'-based naming; kept Synthea verbatim value in 'speciality'.

conflicts.description: Column named 'provider' is described as a foreign key to the organization, conflicting with provider semantics.
conflicts.resolution: Resolved as a provider (clinician) foreign key and merged with omop.visit_occurrence.provider_id, aligned with naming.

conflicts.description: Monetary cost fields are stored as 'string' in Synthea but are numeric quantities.
conflicts.resolution: Cast to 'number' in target (cost).

conflicts.description: OMOP types the birth-date components as 'date', though they are integer calendar components.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'integer' (birth_year, birth_month, birth_day).

conflicts.description: Coordinates typed as 'string' though they are numeric.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'number'.

conflicts.description: Reference-range bounds typed as 'string' though numeric.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'number'.

conflicts.description: Quantity fields typed as 'string' though numeric.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'number'.

conflicts.description: Primary key typed as 'date' instead of an identifier.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'string'.

conflicts.description: Vocabulary name typed as 'integer' though it is text.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'string'.

conflicts.description: Concept identifier typed as 'number' while all sibling concept ids are 'string'.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'string' for consistency.

conflicts.description: Categorical reason flags (D/U/NULL) typed as 'date'.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'string'.

conflicts.description: Concept/monetary fields inconsistently typed as 'integer' while peers are 'string'/'number'.
conflicts.resolution: currency_concept_id retyped to 'string'; paid_patient_coinsurance retyped to 'number'.

conflicts.description: Field described as a datatype indicator (text/numeric) but typed as 'number'.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'string' (value_type).

conflicts.description: Boolean flag fields typed as 'integer'/'string' with values 1/0.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'boolean'.

conflicts.description: Concatenated modifier string typed as 'integer'.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'string'.

conflicts.description: Source coding fields typed as 'integer' though codes may be alphanumeric.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'string'.

conflicts.description: Gender encoded as single letters ('m'/'f') in Synthea vs a standardized gender Concept plus verbatim source value in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Retained 'gender' (verbatim Synthea code) alongside 'gender_concept_id'/'gender_source_value'; scale normalization handled via the concept vocabulary.

conflicts.description: Race/ethnicity are free-text descriptions in Synthea vs standardized multi-column concept+source representations in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Kept Synthea description columns and OMOP concept/source columns side by side; standardized values expressible via the concept table.

conflicts.description: Units are free text in Synthea vs a coded unit concept + verbatim source in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Unified to 'unit_source_value' (verbatim, all sources) plus 'unit_concept_id' (standardized); standard SI units promoted through the concept mapping.

conflicts.description: OMOP monetary values carry an explicit currency concept; Synthea costs carry no currency information.
conflicts.resolution: Cost amounts kept numeric; currency only available through the OMOP cost table, documented as a semantic gap for Synthea-sourced costs.

conflicts.description: Synthea stores native vocabulary codes (SNOMED-CT, RxNorm, LOINC, CVX); OMOP stores both a source value and a mapped standard Concept id.
conflicts.resolution: Synthea codes mapped to '*_source_value' columns and harmonized with OMOP source values; standardized meaning via '*_concept_id'.

conflicts.description: Marital status uses single-letter codes (m/s) with limited coverage (no d/w).
conflicts.resolution: Retained verbatim as 'marital_status' string; no OMOP counterpart column, left as source-specific attribute.

conflicts.description: Temporal granularity differs: Synthea keeps date only; OMOP keeps parallel date and datetime columns.
conflicts.resolution: Both granularities preserved with distinct '*_date'/'*_datetime' columns.

conflicts.description: Synthea denormalizes address attributes into patient/provider/organization rows, whereas OMOP normalizes them into a separate LOCATION table referenced by FK.
conflicts.resolution: Introduced a normalized 'location' resource for OMOP geometry; Synthea address attributes retained as denormalized columns on their owner entities to preserve column-level provenance.

conflicts.description: OMOP uses a paired concept/source representation for coded attributes; Synthea uses a single code+description pair.
conflicts.resolution: Both representations coexisted per attribute (concept_id + source_value + verbatim description) rather than collapsing them.

conflicts.description: OMOP splits observation-type facts and numeric lab measurements into separate tables; Synthea holds them in one table with a value/units/type triple.
conflicts.resolution: Decomposed/normalized into a single unified 'observation' table that captures both textual (value_as_string) and numeric (value_as_number) results.

conflicts.description: Synthea keeps a single full birth date; OMOP keeps a datetime plus extracted year/month/day components.
conflicts.resolution: Kept 'birth_date' plus explicit birth_year/month/day integer components in the unified patient table.

conflicts.description: Synthea models a single encounter; OMOP decomposes visits into visit_occurrence plus a child visit_detail hierarchy.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved both levels as 'encounter' and 'encounter_detail' with a parent-child FK between them.

conflicts.description: Synthea stores death as a single patient attribute; OMOP models a separate 1:1 DEATH table with cause/type concepts.
conflicts.resolution: Folded the 1:1 death record into the 'patient' resource (death_date/datetime, cause and type concepts).

conflicts.description: Synthea imaging studies have no dedicated OMOP table and overlap loosely with procedure/measurement facts.
conflicts.resolution: Retained as a standalone 'imaging_study' resource to avoid lossy forcing into procedure/observation.

conflicts.description: OMOP defines a 1:N relationship between visit_occurrence and visit_detail; Synthea's encounter has no such nesting.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled as encounter (1) to encounter_detail (N) via encounter_id FK; Synthea encounters populate only the parent level.

conflicts.description: Synthea conditions are event-level (1 row per event) while OMOP additionally aggregates events into condition eras (1:N events per era).
conflicts.resolution: Event-level 'condition' retained as canonical; aggregated era structures left to be derived and not conflated with event rows.

conflicts.description: Both describe a many-to-one relationship between providers and the organization/care site they belong to.
conflicts.resolution: Merged both provider-to-organization references into a single 'care_site_id' FK to the 'organization' resource.

conflicts.description: OMOP links a person to a primary care provider (1:1 attribute); Synthea has no such patient-provider link.
conflicts.resolution: Retained patient.provider_id (nullable) sourced only from OMOP; no Synthea provenance.

conflicts.description: OMOP defines one-to-many person-to-coverage and person-to-observation-period relationships that Synthea lacks.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled as separate child resources (payer_plan_period, observation_period) keyed to patient.

conflicts.description: Several Synthea tables (allergies, conditions, medications, procedures, observations, immunizations) declare no primary key.
conflicts.resolution: OMOP surrogate keys adopted where available; purely synthetic surrogate keys (e.g., allergy_id, immunization_id) introduced only for target mechanics and marked with empty provenance.

conflicts.description: Primary key identification differs: Synthea relies on a generic 'id' while OMOP uses explicit entity-scoped keys, and some OMOP keys were mistyped.
conflicts.resolution: Harmonized to a single snake_case '<entity>_id' key per unified resource, with both source keys listed in provenance.

conflicts.description: Synthea's encounter 'provider' column ambiguously references an organization, whereas OMOP separates provider_id and care_site_id foreign keys.
conflicts.resolution: Resolved as a provider clinician FK (provider_id) and retained a distinct care_site_id FK to organization.

conflicts.description: Synthea expresses foreign keys as bare columns (patient, encounter) with no declared key relationships.
conflicts.resolution: Reconstructed explicit foreign keys (patient_id, encounter_id, provider_id) referencing the unified parent resources.

conflicts.description: payer_plan_period_id was declared with a non-identifier type, weakening key identification.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to 'string' and promoted to the primary key of 'payer_plan_period'.

conflicts.description: OMOP uses polymorphic 'event_id' + '*_event_field_concept_id' keys whose target entity is data-dependent.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved as generic event id plus field concept id (not resolvable as a static FK), documented as a polymorphic relationship.
